entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Complexity in wallet software design poses significant challenges, particularly when it comes to supporting various script templates and ensuring compatibility with evolving Bitcoin features. Wallets currently operate by signing a pre-defined set of script templates, typically without parsing the scripts themselves. This design choice simplifies implementation and reduces the potential for errors. The introduction of new script versions or additional complexity does not alleviate these challenges for core implementations like bitcoind, as they must retain support for all previous versions, perpetually increasing their complexity.
Minimalism in wallet architecture is crucial due to the already suboptimal state of many existing Bitcoin wallets. Emphasizing simplicity in future wallet designs can mitigate risks and enhance usability, especially since wallets are not required to maintain legacy support in the same way as full node software. Practical experience has shown that losses of funds are rarely attributed to the reuse of private keys between Lightning Network operations and other activities. More commonly, trivial mistakes such as reusing payment hashes across invoices are responsible for security lapses and fund losses.
The successful implementation of BIP 143, thanks to its clarity and straightforwardness, demonstrates the importance of clear technical guidance. A simple, naive approach was sufficient for Segwit integration, underscoring that wallet developers benefit from concise and unambiguous protocols. As the ecosystem evolves, prioritizing simplicity and clarity in wallet standards will be essential for both user safety and developer efficiency. For further reading on the topic, refer to the discussion at [lists.linuxfoundation.org](https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/pipermail/bitcoin-dev/2018-December/016523.html).
